newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus approves Kirch TV stake swap.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus approves Kirch TV stake swap.

text.p: French pay television group Canal Plus said Wednesday its board has approved a stake swap with German media mogul Leo Kirch.
Details will be published after a deal is finalised in the next few days, it said.

Canal said its supervisory board is allowing management to sell the company's 37.5 percent stake in German pay-television company Premiere to the Kirch group. It also approved the acquisition from Kirch of 45 percent in Italy's Telepiu.

Premiere is currently owned by Canal Plus , Kirch and Bertelsmann. The sale of the stake by Canal Plus would allow the French group to leave the German market while the two German companies can control the pay televison service.
Only a year ago, Kirsch and Premiere were bitter rivals working on separate plans to launch digital satellite television services.
Canal Plus already owns a 45 percent stake in Telepiu following its merger with Nethold.

Analysts had estimated the value of Canal Plus' Premiere stake at between 1.7 billion ($288.1 million) and 2.4 billion francs ($406.8 million), and Kirch's Telepiu stake at between 1.3 billion ($220.3 million) and 1.4 billion francs ($237.3 million).
They expect Canal Plus to get a cash payment of around 900 million francs ($152.5 million).
